Subject: Thanks — follow-up on retention exceptions (Acme Health)

Hi Jamie — thanks again for the call today. Quick summary + proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

- Ask: Acme needs a 0-retention policy for user-generated content that may contain PHI/PII (no stored full-text logs).
- Ask caveat: Legal indicated a potential need for short-lived transcripts for dispute resolution/QA (you mentioned ~30 days).
- Live suggestion: We can offer an exception path where content is not persisted and only anonymized/metadata-level audit logs are retained. If transcripts are required, we can store them encrypted for a customer-specified retention window (e.g., 30 days) and then auto-delete.

Attached: Data_Retention_Appendix_v2.pdf (draft of technical controls we discussed).

Can you confirm: 1) whether Acme is willing to accept a 30-day transcript retention for operational needs, and 2) whether Legal would sign an exception / addendum? If yes, I’ll loop in Security and CS to scope implementation and produce a redline.

Thanks — I’ll book a 30-min follow-up once we have confirmation.

—Camila

Thanks Camila — good summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Acme cannot accept any persistent storage of PHI-containing chat transcripts beyond what is strictly necessary for safety/compliance.
- Our Legal team is open to a technical exception where the vendor (you) prevents long-term storage of content and implements strong access controls.
- For operational/legal reasons we need a short retention window for full-session transcripts (30 days max) to support incident investigations and customer disputes.

I’ve looped in Legal; they’ll review any proposed addendum. Please have Security confirm the controls (redaction, encryption, access logs) and CS provide how we’d operate the deletion flow.

-Jamie

Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data retention exception (Acme Health) — security controls

Camila — thanks for the context. High level security stance / recommended controls: 

- Content handling: default policy = ephemeral (no persistent full-text logs in our hosted tenancy). All generated tokens and user inputs are ephemeral unless a retention flag is enabled.
- Transcript option: implement encrypted object store with customer-provided KMS; retention policy enforced at storage layer (auto-delete lifecycle, 30 days default).
- Redaction: PII/PHI detection + optional deterministic masking before any transcript storage.
- Audit logs: maintain minimal meta-logs (timestamps, request IDs, route, truncated token counts) in a separate, access-controlled audit index. No user content in audit logs.
- Access controls & attestations: role-based access, signed access logs, and SOC2 appendix (attached).

Open items we’ll need from Acme to produce final language: 
- Who owns the KMS (Acme-managed or Redwood-managed with customer key)?
- Which roles at Acme should be permitted to request transcript exports?
- Any specific legal phrases they require for the exception (Jamie, Legal to provide).

I’ll draft a controls one-pager and a suggested addendum clause. Rafael — can you confirm operational feasibility for Dedicated pilot and S3 export?

—Neha
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data retention exception (Acme Health) — ops notes + pilot plan

Quick ops summary / how we’d run the pilot: 

- Environment: Dedicated pool for Acme (isolated GPUs), network controls (VPC peering), optional on-prem connector if requested.
- Storage: support customer-managed S3 buckets; implement lifecycle rule to auto-delete objects after N days (configurable). We can set default 30d.
- Logging: set to metadata-only in the customer tenancy. Full transcripts only written when transcript retention is toggled for a session or flagged by admin.
- Redaction: pipeline supports pre-store redaction for PII types we surface (SSNs, emails, phone numbers). We can provide both deterministic masks and hashed tokens depending on their preference.
- Cost/Timeline: pilot (2-3 weeks) + production roll (2-4 weeks). Additional monthly cost: ~$1.5k for dedicated pool + storage costs tied to retention volume.

I’ve added a draft pilot checklist in the SharePoint doc: https://redwoodinference.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/teams/legal/Retention-Appendix. Rafael — assigning the Canaries/ops runbook to you.

—Marissa
From: Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Data retention exception (Acme Health) — redlines attached

Camila/Team — Attached is Acme’s redline to the retention appendix (AcmeHealth_Retention_Redline.docx). Key asks from Legal: 

1) Explicit clause: No full-text content retention in vendor systems except for transcripts retained <= 30 days and explicitly permitted by Acme.
2) Customer-controlled KMS required for any transcript storage containing PHI.
3) Auditability: vendor must provide signed, time-stamped access logs on request and notify Acme of any access within 48 hours.
4) Right to audit + SOC2 report delivery on an annual basis.

If Redwood can accept these with minor edits we’ll route to our GC for signature. Please confirm acceptance by Tuesday so we can proceed.

—Acme Legal
